Source: Sabbat Guide

The Sabbat, who name themselves the Sword of Caine, are the vampires of the Great Jyhad: a holy war against the Antediluvians, the ancient and monstrous progenitors of the clans, and against the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}, whom the Sabbat brand as the Antediluvians' unwitting servants. The sect was born out of the Anarch Revolt, when rebellious neonates of Clans @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} destroyed their own Antediluvians and shattered the old elder-dominated order. Rather than accept the peace of the Convention of Thorns that followed, these anarchs chose endless war instead, convinced that the only way to escape the fate of being drained or devoured by their monstrous forebears at Gehenna is to strike first and never stop striking. Where the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} clings to the Masquerade and the pretense of humanity, the Sabbat has embraced its damnation. Its members consider themselves already lost to the Beast, and rather than mourn their humanity, they flaunt their monstrosity as a mark of freedom.

The sect is led rather than ruled, and its hierarchy is loose and often resented by the young Cainites who do most of its fighting. At the base of Sabbat society is the pack, a tight surrogate family of vampires bound to one another through shared ritual; a Sabbat vampire belongs to only one pack at a time, usually the one that performed her Creation Rites. Each pack is led by a Ductus, whose authority may come from brute dominance, ritual combat, or genuine respect, and who handles the pack's day-to-day and logistical decisions. Alongside the Ductus stands the pack's Priest, its spiritual leader, who administers rites such as the Vaulderie and oversees the pack's religious observances. Above individual packs, a Bishop maintains Sabbat influence within a city, sometimes compared to a Camarilla primogen, while an Archbishop rules an entire city outright and also serves as its spiritual authority. Cardinals oversee whole territories and the archbishops within them, and at the very top sits the Regent, the sect's sole recognized leader, of whom only one exists at any time. Templars occupy a position outside this chain of command entirely, acting as impartial enforcers of Sabbat law answerable to their specific duties rather than to local politics.

No practice binds the Sabbat together more than the Vaulderie: the mingled blood of every vampire in a pack, consecrated by the pack priest and drunk by all members together. It creates a vinculum, an artificial blood tie of loyalty between packmates, and is performed again and again - before battle, after crisis, or simply as nightly ritual - to keep a pack unified. New members are brought into the sect through the Creation Rites, in which a priest brands the initiate's forehead with a flaming brand while she swears an oath of loyalty to her pack, its chain of command, and the Sabbat itself; the rite is capped with a Vaulderie shared among the new packmates.

Culturally, the Sabbat prizes violence, zealotry, and pack loyalty above all else, and its members reject the Road of Humanity in favor of the various Paths of Enlightenment - inhuman codes such as the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.db3Fhvpv32rhN3Mm]{Path of Caine}, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.aSh4ybe4GTvTn7LR]{Path of the Feral Heart}, and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.MkHKLOcOCLQ5pWCj]{Path of Honorable Accord} - each of which exalts some aspect of vampiric nature rather than clinging to a lost mortality. This is a sect that treats its own dissolution as unthinkable even as corruption and infighting eat at it from within, one where elders often manipulate zealous neonates into fighting the Jyhad in their place. Distinctive rites mark its calendar and its justice alike: the War Party pits packs against one another to hunt and diablerize an elder Kindred for glory and status, while the Wild Hunt turns the Vaulderie and fire against traitors within the sect's own ranks.

Auctoritas Ritae are the sect's thirteen core sacred rituals, upheld with the reverence of commandments - including the Vaulderie and Creation Rites already noted, alongside rites such as the Fire Dance, the Palla Grande (Grand Ball), and the Blood Bath. During the Fire Dance, Sabbat vampires prove their loyalty and courage by leaping through raging bonfires, a display of mastery over the fear of flame that often opens war efforts and other major sect gatherings. The Palla Grande, also called the Grand Ball, is a masquerade-style festival in which a presiding priest prepares hallucinogenic incense to weaken mortal guests' inhibitions before the ritus culminates in the Blood Bath: an archbishop or ranking bishop reclines in a vessel filled with the blood of drained victims mixed with vitae from a communal Vaulderie cup, absorbing something of the assembled pack's essence.

Disputes within the sect are frequently settled through Monomacy, a formal ritual duel fought under strict rules and sanctioned by a pack priest, often ending in the Final Death of the loser. Rather than being viewed as mere violence, Monomacy is treated as a form of internal evolutionary selection, purging members deemed too weak or misguided to serve the sect's ends; the duels can take unusual forms, from chess-like contests using living pieces to firearms duels fought through intermediary ghouls. The victor claims the loser's possessions (barring diablerie, unless the priest permits it), and even leadership positions such as the regency have reportedly changed hands this way.

The Black Hand is the Sabbat's secretive militia, a specialized military force organized into permanent nomadic "columns" and tasked with waging the sect's wars; all Sabbat are sworn to support it under the Code of Milan, though Templars (paladins) are explicitly barred from joining, since their loyalty must remain to their individual charges rather than factional politics. Other notable customs include the Festivo dell'Estinto ("Festival of the Dead"), a citywide gathering held each April drawing in nomadic packs as well as founded covens, and the practice of headhunting, in which some Sabbat collect the skulls of formidable slain enemies - vampire, Lupine, or hunter alike - as marks of honor.
